title: IT mistake erases 11 years of viewing history for hospitals’ maternity records
gist: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (NUH) overwrote 11 years (September 2011-November 2022) of maternity-record access-log data on August 18 after running a pre-written database-copy script intended for a radiotherapy system against a maternity database instead, and cannot fully restore who viewed the records; the incident lands amid a separate police probe into 500+ maternity harm cases and a prior 2025 'intentional or malicious' record deletion.

themes.theme: Root cause and scope of the data loss

insights.claim: NUH's data loss stemmed from a script reused from a different hospital system: a setting that should have been changed before running the process to copy a radiotherapy database was missed, so the process ran on and overwrote the maternity records database instead.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A textbook case of unvalidated script reuse across environments causing catastrophic data loss — a governance/change-management failure pattern relevant to any IT-operations risk assessment of healthcare or regulated-data systems.
insights.quote: The process used a set of pre-written computer instructions that had previously been used for a different hospital system. A setting that should have been changed before the process was run was missed.

insights.claim: The overwritten database held maternity records access-history data for NUH patients from September 2011 to November 2022, and the hospital has been unable to restore the complete access-history log, meaning it generally cannot confirm whether a given maternity record was viewed by a particular person during that 11-year span.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Loss of access-audit trails (not clinical data itself) undermines the ability to investigate potential unauthorized record access retroactively, a compliance/legal exposure for the trust.
insights.quote: we have not been able to restore the complete history showing who viewed maternity records during this period
insights.locator: NUH has been unable to retrieve some of the data

insights.claim: NUH says it escalated the issue within minutes of being identified, worked with external specialists to recover as much data as possible, and was able to restore actual patient care-related data (notes, observations, test results), with no patient information accessed or used inappropriately as a result.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Distinguishes clinical-data integrity (preserved) from audit-log integrity (lost), an important nuance for assessing the actual severity of the breach versus its reputational/regulatory optics.
insights.quote: No patient information was accessed or used inappropriately as a result of this incident
insights.locator: NUH noted that the data loss doesn’t impact current patient care

themes.theme: Broader context: NUH maternity scandal and prior incidents

insights.claim: This data loss comes amid a broader police investigation into allegations that over 500 mothers and babies suffered 'potentially avoidable' harm or died due to systemic failings at NUH, per a June review led by a senior midwife citing understaffing, undertrained employees, and failure to listen to parental concerns.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Positions this IT failure within a much larger institutional crisis at NUH, raising the stakes of any further data or process failures and increasing regulatory/legal risk exposure for the trust.
insights.locator: The announcement comes as NUH faces a broader police investigation

insights.claim: In June 2025, a separate local police investigation concluded that a file with records for hundreds of maternity care patients at NUH was likely erased 'intentionally or maliciously,' though NUH recovered that data days after deletion; Nottinghamshire Police is now investigating whether the new data loss connects to the larger maternity harm case.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A prior deliberate deletion incident plus this new accidental one within roughly a year raises questions about NUH's IT security and change-control maturity that could affect its standing with regulators (CQC, ICO) and funding.
insights.locator: Also, in June 2025, a local police investigation concluded
